title: Final: exact geometry
sub: B-rep, tessellation, STEP and DWG: test yourself
cards/0/task: Prepare the cylinder for the web: deviation of 0.1 mm or less and no more than 260 triangles.
cards/1/q: How is a cylinder in STEP different from a cylinder in GLB?
cards/1/options/0: STEP has the formula “radius 50 mm”; GLB has a set of triangles
cards/1/explain: STEP stores the exact surface; GLB stores an approximation of it.
cards/2/task: Turn the Bézier curve into an exact quarter circle.
cards/3/q: The segment count went up 3 times. The tessellation error dropped by about…
cards/3/explain: The error falls with the square of the segment count.
cards/4/q: Where is the exact surface here?
cards/4/explain: SPHERICAL_SURFACE with radius 25 is an exact sphere. The rest is its coordinate system.
cards/5/q: Which of these are exact CAD geometry? Select all.
cards/6/q: A drawing from a new AutoCAD will not open for a colleague with an old one. What do you do?
cards/6/options/0: Save to an older DWG version or send a DXF
cards/6/explain: AutoCAD can “Save As” older DWG versions.
cards/7/q: What does the angular tolerance give you in tessellation?
cards/7/options/0: Small circles get split finely enough even when the chordal deviation is already met
cards/7/explain: The angle limits how much neighboring triangles can differ in slope.
